_comment: C10 machine-turn corpus, shared by the three gates that must agree: the lib's Test-MachineTurnPrompt (daemon + inline PowerShell paths), the compiled client's stdin scan (mem0-hook-client.cs) and the server's hook_contract.is_machine_turn_prompt. Shapes are the REAL UserPromptSubmit hook inputs, scrubbed: a background task notification reaches the hook with its prompt starting with <task-notification>, both when it is its own turn (transcript user record, origin.kind=task-notification) and when it was queued behind a running turn (transcript queued_command attachment, commandMode=task-notification). Sampled hook-input fixtures matched the queued_command prompt byte-for-byte, so a queued notification uses the SAME wrapper. Peer messages from another session (cross-session-message / agent-message) are NOT task notifications and stay human-path on purpose.

prompts.name: task notification, own turn (background command finished)
prompts.prompt:
<task-notification>
<task-id>b0c1d2e3f</task-id>
<tool-use-id>toolu_01AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA</tool-use-id>
<output-file>C:\Users\__WIN_USER__\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\example-project\00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001\tasks\b0c1d2e3f.output</output-file>
<status>completed</status>
<summary>Background command "Run the stress test under a drained lease (30 min)" completed (exit code 0)</summary>
</task-notification>

prompts.name: task notification, queued behind a running turn (agent finished)
prompts.prompt:
<task-notification>
<task-id>a6cf7de54213ef878</task-id>
<tool-use-id>toolu_01BBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBB</tool-use-id>
<output-file>C:\Users\__WIN_USER__\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\example-project\00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002\tasks\a6cf7de54213ef878.output</output-file>
<status>completed</status>
<summary>Agent "Review the self-heal scripts" finished</summary>
<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own.</note>
<result>No blockers. You missed nothing; revert is not needed. The admission gate and the memory stack both hold.</result>
</task-notification>

prompts.name: task notification, queued monitor event
prompts.prompt:
<task-notification>
<task-id>bi7dkqg03</task-id>
<summary>Monitor event: "stress run started or failed to start"</summary>
<event>stress-20260922-131402.txt</event>
</task-notification>

prompts.name: task notification after leading whitespace
prompts.prompt:
<task-notification>
<task-id>b9z8y7x6w</task-id>
<status>stopped</status>
<summary>Background workflow "context audit" did not finish before the previous session ended</summary>
</task-notification>

prompts.name: human prompt (substantive)
prompts.prompt: what is the state of the admission gate and the memory stack deploy

prompts.name: human prompt that quotes a notification mid-text
prompts.prompt: why did this <task-notification> fire twice for the memory stack job?

prompts.name: human prompt carrying a slash-command wrapper
near-miss tag is not the notification wrapper
prompts.prompt: <task-notifications> are they noisy in the memory stack logs?

prompts.name: cross-session peer message (not a task notification)
prompts.prompt:
Another Claude session sent a message:
<cross-session-message from="uds:example">please check the memory stack deploy</cross-session-message>
